Rashi on Eruvin 67a:10:1.hebrew: אליבא דמ"ד - לעיל בפירקין (עירובין דף סה:), היכא דאתי נכרי בשבת שוכרין הימנו ואח"כ מבטלין — לא תיבעי לך:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:10:1.english: In accordance with the one who said - Earlier in our chapter (Eruvin 65b), [that] where a gentile arrives on Shabbat, one may rent from him and subsequently renounce [rights] — you have no dilemma.

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:10:2.hebrew: השתא תרתי עבדינן - שכירות וביטול, חדא מיבעיא:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:10:2.english: Now that we perform two - Rental and renunciation [of rights] — is one [alone] a question?

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:11:1.hebrew: אני אומר מבטלין - ולא דמיא לההיא דלעיל, דהכא, אי בעי מיגר וערובי מאתמול — מצי עבדי:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:11:1.english: I say one may renounce [rights] - And it is not similar to that [case] above, for here, had they wanted to rent and establish an eiruv yesterday, they could have done so.

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:11:2.hebrew: והמנונא אמר אין מבטלין - כיון דאי בעו ערובי מאתמול, לא מצי עבדי בלא שכירות — אין ביטול אלא במקום עירוב:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:11:2.english: And [Rav] Hamnuna said: One may not renounce - Since, if they had wanted to make an eruv yesterday, they could not have done [so] without renting — [and] there is no renunciation [of rights] except in a place where an eruv [could take effect].

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:13:1.english: That one is preferable to him - Because there is more fresh air than in an alleyway.

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:14:1.english: [Citing] a tradition - That he heard [it] from his teacher, and his teacher from his teacher.

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:1:1.hebrew: שכח אחד מן החיצונה ולא עירב - בהא מודי שמואל דמבטלי בני חיצונה לבני פנימית אותו רשות שבא להן לתוכן ע"י הרגל עירובן, משום דאמר לה: "לתקוני שתפתיך ולא לעוותי", והכי מפרש לה בסוף פירקין. והא דבעינן ביטול, אליבא דרבי עקיבא אמרה רבא למילתיה; דאי לרבנן, בלאו ביטול נמי אמרה לה פנימית הכי ועקרה לה לעירוב משום דמעוותי בה, אבל ר"ע אמר דבעיא לבטולי בשילהי פירקין. וכי שכח בן פנימית, ליכא למימר הכי — דליבטל לבני פנימית ותיחוד דשא ותשמש — דלא מצי למימר "לתקוני שתפתיך ולא לעוותי", שהרי תחילת העיוות ע"י בן פנימי בא:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:1:1.english: [If] a resident of the outer [courtyard] forgot and did not establish an eiruv - In this [case], Shmuel concedes that the residents of the outer [courtyard] can renounce in favor of the residents of the inner [courtyard] that right [of domain] that accrued to them in it through the access [granted by] their eiruv, because [the inner courtyard] says to it: “I partnered with you to improve, and not to cause detriment.” And so [the Gemara] explains it at the end of our chapter. And this [ruling] that we require renunciation — Rava stated his statement in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Akiva; for according to the Rabbis, even without renunciation the inner [courtyard] says this to it and uproots the eiruv, because they are causing detriment to it; whereas Rabbi Akiva says that it requires renunciation, at the end of our chapter. And when a resident of the inner [courtyard] forgot, it is not possible to say this — that he should renounce [his rights] in favor of the residents of the inner [courtyard], and it should close the door and use [its courtyard] — for it cannot say “I partnered with you to improve, and not to cause detriment,” as the start of the detriment came about through a resident of the inner [courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:3:1.hebrew: כמאן כר' אליעזר - רבא קא מהדר ליה לרב הונא: כמאן קאמרת למילתך — כר"א, דאמר אינו צריך כו'? בשילהי עושין פסין אוקימנא הכי:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:3:1.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer - Rava is replying to Rav Huna: In accordance with whose [opinion] do you say your statement — in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who said, “It is not necessary...” etc.? At the end of [the chapter] Osin Passin, we established it like this.

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:4:1.hebrew: ממתנייתא דרב ששת - שהיו משניות סדורות לו, וירא רב חסדא שלא יקשה ממשנה על משנה ויאמר לו לתרצן:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:4:1.english: From the teachings of Rav Sheshet - For the Mishnayot were well ordered for him, and Rav Ḥisda feared that he would raise a contradiction from one Mishnah against another Mishnah and tell him to resolve them.

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:4:2.hebrew: מפלפוליה - חריף וסבר היה ביותר, ועמוק בשאילותיו:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:4:2.english: From his sharpness - He was exceedingly sharp and analytical, and profound in his questions.

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:5:1.hebrew: והקיפום - סתמו רה"ר מכאן ומכאן, ונשאר לפני ב' הבתים כעין חצר שהבתים פתוחות לה:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:5:1.english: And enclosed them - They blocked the public domain on both sides, and there remained in front of the two houses a kind of courtyard to which the houses open:

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:5:2.hebrew: מהו - שיבטל זה רשותו לזה, ויהא מותר להוציא מביתו לכאן? דהא קיי"ל בפירקא תניינא (דף כ.): כל מחיצות הנעשות בשבת, בין בשוגג בין במזיד, שמה מחיצה, וכ"ש הכא דנכרים עבדוה:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:5:2.english: What is [the halakha] - Can this [resident] renounce his domain to that [resident], and it will be permitted to carry out from his house to here? For behold, we maintain in the second chapter (daf 20a): Any partitions made on Shabbat, whether unwittingly or intentionally, are considered a [valid] partition, and all the more so here, where gentiles made it.

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:6:1.hebrew: אליבא דמאן דאמר אין ביטול רשות מחצר לחצר - ואוקימנא טעמא משום דאין אוסרין ואין מבטלין, ואע"ג דאי בעו לעירובי הוו מערבי — אלמא תרתי בעינן: אוסרין ומערבין:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:6:1.english: In accordance with the one who said there is no renouncing of rights from courtyard to courtyard - And we established the reason [earlier] as being that [since] they do not restrict [one another], they do not renounce [their rights], even though had they wanted to establish an *eiruv* they could have established an *eiruv*; evidently, we require two [conditions]: [that they] restrict and establish an *eiruv*.

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:6:2.hebrew: לא תיבעי לך - דכ"ש, דהכא לא הא ולא הא — דלא הוו אוסרין זה על זה אתמול, ולא תורת עירוב היתה לכאן:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:6:2.english: You have no dilemma - For all the more so [is it clear], as here neither this nor that [applied]: they did not restrict one another yesterday, nor did the rule of an eiruv apply here.

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:7:1.hebrew: כי תיבעי לך אליבא דמאן דאמר יש ביטול - ואע"ג דאין אוסרין, מאי? מי אמרינן: התם הוא דאי בעו לערובי הוו מערבי, ואע"ג דתרתי ליכא — חדא מיהא איכא; אבל הכא, דאפילו חדא ליכא — לא? או דילמא: מדאהא לא קפיד, אהא נמי לא קפיד:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:7:1.english: Where you have a dilemma is in accordance with the one who said, "There is renouncing" - And [granted that renouncing is effective] even though they do not prohibit [each other], what [is the dilemma]? Do we say: It is [specifically] there that [renouncing is effective], because had they wanted to establish an eiruv, they could have established an eiruv, and even though both [conditions] are not [met], at least one [of them] is present; but here, where not even one [condition] is present, [renouncing is] not [effective]? Or perhaps, since [the law] does not insist on this [condition], it does not insist on that [condition] either?

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:8:1.english: One may not renounce - For we require at least one [condition to be met].

Rashi on Eruvin 67a:9:1.hebrew: מת נכרי בשבת - הא נמי בעא מיניה: שני ישראלים ונכרי הדרים בחצר, ולא שכרו ולא עירבו, ומת נכרי בשבת — מהו לבטל זה לזה:
Rashi on Eruvin 67a:9:1.english: A gentile died on Shabbat - This, too, [Rav Ḥisda] asked of him: [In the case of] two Jews and a gentile who reside in a courtyard, and they did not rent [from the gentile] and did not make an eiruv, and the gentile died on Shabbat — what is [the halakha]: may they renounce [their rights] to one another?

Tosafot on Eruvin 67a:11:1.hebrew: אני אומר מבטלין - פי' בקונטרס: דלא דמיא לההיא דלעיל היכא דאתא נכרי בשבתא, דהכא, אי בעו מיגר וערובי מאתמול — מצו עבדי. ורב המנונא אמר: אין מבטלין, כיון דאי בעו לערובי מאתמול, לא מצו מערבי בלא שכירות — אין ביטול אלא במקום עירוב. עד כאן לשון הקונט'. ותימה, דלעיל (עירובין דף סו.) פשיטא לן היכא דאתא נכרי מאתמול דמבטלין, ו"אוסרין ומערבין" קרינן ביה, דאמר לעיל: "ואי דאתא נכרי מאתמול, לוגר מאתמול"! י"ל: דסוגיא דלעיל כרב ששת, דאמר הכא דמבטלין. ומיהו קשה, דמשמע הכא דפשיטא לן, אפי' לרב ששת, דתרתי לא עבדינן, ודוקא מת הוא דמבטלין, אבל לא מת, דבעי תרתי — שכירות וביטול — לא עבדינן; ולעיל פשיטא לן בדאתא מאתמול דבשבת שוכרין ומבטלין, ודוקא באתא בשבת קאמר שמואל דאין מבטלין! ונראה לפרש: דהכא, באתא בשבת ומת בשבת איירי. וכן משמע הלשון, דקאמר: "כי תיבעי לך אליבא דמאן דאמר אין שוכרין, תרתי הוא דלא עבדינן" — ובאתא נכרי בשבת נחלקו; ועל זה מיבעיא ליה: כשמת, אי עבדינן חדא אי לא. וא"ת: כי לא מת נמי תסגי בחדא, בביטול לחודיה, דהוה יחיד במקום נכרי? וי"ל: כדפי' לעיל, דלא משתרי בביטול לחודיה כשמתרצה הנכרי לשכור, כיון דאם לא היה מתרצה לא היה מותר, משום דאם כן בטלת תורת עירוב. אי נמי: רב חסדא כר' מאיר סבירא ליה, דאסר יחיד במקום נכרי. ומיהו לפי טעם זה אחרון, לא יתכן לומר "אליבא דמאן דאמר אין שוכרין" דקאמר (אני אומר מבטלין) — היינו שמואל; דממה נפשך: לשמואל סגי בביטול, דאיהו קאמר הלכה כראב"י, וקאמר שמואל לעיל דאין מבטלין, ש"מ דאפי' חדא לא עבדינן לשמואל; אלא היינו ר' אסי, דאמר לעיל "לא נשכור":
Tosafot on Eruvin 67a:11:1.english: "I say that they may renounce" - The Kunteres explained that [this case] is not similar to that [case] above where the gentile arrived on Shabbat; for here, had they wanted to rent and establish an eiruv yesterday, they could have done so. And Rav Hamnuna said that they may not renounce, since had they wanted to establish an eiruv yesterday, they could not have established an eiruv without rental, [and] there is no renunciation except in a place of an eiruv. Until here is the wording of the Kunteres. And [this is] astonishing, for above (Eruvin 66a) it was obvious to us that where the gentile arrived yesterday, they may renounce, and we apply to him [the rule of] "those who restrict and establish an eiruv" — as [the Gemara] said above: "And if the gentile arrived yesterday, let him rent yesterday!" One can say that the sugya above is in accordance with Rav Sheshet, who says here that they may renounce. However, it is difficult, for it implies here that it is obvious to us, even according to Rav Sheshet, that we do not perform two [actions on Shabbat], and it is specifically [when the gentile] died that they may renounce, but if he did not die, where two [actions] are required — rental and renunciation — we do not perform [them]; whereas above, it was obvious to us regarding [a gentile] who arrived yesterday that on Shabbat they rent and renounce, and only when he arrived on Shabbat did Shmuel say that they do not renounce! And it seems [correct] to explain that here, [the Gemara] is dealing with [a gentile who] arrived on Shabbat and died on Shabbat. And so implies the wording, as it says: "When your dilemma arises, it is according to the one who said they do not rent: Is it two [actions] that we do not perform..." — and it was regarding [a gentile who] arrived on Shabbat that they disagreed; and regarding this the dilemma was raised: when he died, do we perform one [action] or not? And if you say: Even when he did not die, let one [action] suffice, renunciation alone, since he would be an individual [Jew] in the place of a gentile [which is permitted according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov]? And one can say: As [I] explained above, it is not permitted through renunciation alone when the gentile is willing to rent, since had he not been willing [to rent], it would not be permitted, because if so, you would abolish the concept of eiruv. Alternatively, Rav Ḥisda holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who prohibited an individual [Jew] in the place of a gentile. However, according to this latter reason, it is not possible to say that [the statement], "In accordance with the one who said they do not rent," which [the Gemara] stated ("I say that they may renounce"), is [referring to] Shmuel; for whichever way you look at it: according to Shmuel, renunciation [alone] would suffice, since he said that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, yet Shmuel said above that they do not renounce — learn from this that even one [action] we do not perform according to Shmuel! Rather, this [one who said they do not rent] is Rabbi Asi, who said above, "We shall not rent."

Tosafot on Eruvin 67a:11:2.hebrew: אני אומר מבטלין - אף על גב דבשני בתים אין מבטלין — התם ליכא לא אוסרין ולא מערבין, שהיא רה"ר מבעוד יום; אבל הכא, אוסרין איכא, וגם מערבין עד שיבא הנכרי. א"נ: גבי שני בתים לא היה לו כח מבעוד יום לעשות אותו ביטול שעושה עכשיו, אבל הכא, מבעוד יום היה בו כח לבטל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 67a:11:2.english: "I say they may renounce" - Even though in [the case of] two houses [on opposite sides of a public domain enclosed on Shabbat] they may not renounce [their rights — there], there is neither [mutual] restriction nor [the ability to] join with an eruv, as it was a public domain while it was still day; but here, there is [mutual] restriction, and they could also join with an eruv until the gentile would arrive. Alternatively: regarding the two houses, he did not have the power while it was still day to perform that renunciation which he performs now; but here, while it was still day he had the power to renounce.

Tosafot on Eruvin 67a:1:1.hebrew: שכח אחד מבני חיצונה ולא עירב עמהן - בהא מודה שמואל, דמבטלין בני חיצונה לבני הפנימית אותו רשות שיש להן בתוכן על ידי הרגל עירובן, משום דאמרה: "לתקוני שתפתיך ולא לעוותי", והכי מפרש בשילהי פירקין. והא דבעיא ביטול — אליבא דר"ע אמר רבא למילתיה; דאי לרבנן, בלא ביטול נמי אמרי לה לפנימית הכי, ועקרה לעירוב' משום דמעוותי לה, אבל ר' עקיבא — דבעי לבטולי בשילהי פירקין. וכי שכח אחד מן הפנימית, ליכא למימר הכי — לבטל לבני פנימית, ותיחוד דשא ותשמש — דלא מצי למימר "לתקוני שתפתיך ולא לעוותי" דבעיא ביטול, שהרי תחילת [העיוות] ע"י בן הפנימית הוא בא. כל זה לשון הקונט'. וא"ת: ורבא מנא ליה דשמואל מוקי לה כר"ע, דבעי' ביטול? דלמא כרבנן, דשרו לקמן בלא ביטול? וי"ל: משום דשמעינן ליה לשמואל דאמר: "אוסרין, ומערבין, ומבטלין — ב' חצירות זו לפנים מזו", ולא מתוקם אלא בהכי. וא"ת: וכי שכח אחד מבני פנימית ולא עירב, ומבטל לבני פנימית, אמאי אתיא חיצונה ואסרה עלייהו משום עירוב המרגילה לתוכה? הא אמר לעיל בפרק מי שהוציאוהו (עירובין דף מח:): "דלא אמרו דיורין להחמיר"! י"ל: דההיא דלעיל ליכא שום פשיעותה, אבל הכא הפנימית פשעה ועותה את עצמה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 67a:1:1.english: If one of the residents of the outer [courtyard] forgot and did not establish an eiruv with them - In this [case], Shmuel concedes that the residents of the outer [courtyard] may renounce in favor of the residents of the inner [courtyard] that right [of entry] that they possess into their [courtyard] on account of the access afforded by their eiruv, because [the inner courtyard] can say: "I partnered with you to improve [my situation], not to worsen [it]"; and this is explained at the end of our chapter. And as for this [requirement] that renunciation is needed, Rava stated his statement according to Rabbi Akiva; for according to the Rabbis, even without renunciation, [the residents] say this to the inner [courtyard], and it uproots its eiruv because [the outer courtyard] worsens [her situation]. But Rabbi Akiva requires renunciation at the end of our chapter. And when one of the [residents of the] inner [courtyard] forgot [to establish an eiruv], one cannot say this — that he should renounce [his rights] to the residents of the inner [courtyard], and it could close the door and use [its courtyard] — as [the inner courtyard] cannot say: "I partnered with you to improve [my situation], not to worsen [it]" [such that renunciation would be effective], for the onset of the detriment came about through a resident of the inner [courtyard]. All this is the phrasing of the Kuntres [Rashi]. And if you say: And from where did Rava know that Shmuel established [this] according to Rabbi Akiva, who requires renunciation? Perhaps [Shmuel established it] according to the Rabbis, who permit [it] later on [in the chapter] without renunciation? And one can answer: Because we have heard Shmuel say: "Two courtyards, one within the other, forbid [each other], establish an eiruv [together], and renounce [rights to each other]"; and it can only be established in this manner. And if you say: And when one of the residents of the inner [courtyard] forgot and did not establish an eiruv, and [then] renounces [his rights] to the residents of the inner [courtyard], why does the outer [courtyard] come and forbid [carrying] to them on account of the eiruv that accustomed it [to enter] into it? But didn't [the Gemara] say earlier in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehotziuho (Eruvin 48b) that they did not state [the principle of] residents to be stringent?! One can answer: In that [case] earlier, there is no negligence whatsoever; but here, the inner [courtyard] was negligent and caused damage to itself.

Tosafot on Eruvin 67a:3:1.hebrew: כמאן כר' אליעזר כו' - לעיל בשמעתין, כשנתנו עירובן בחיצונה ושכח א' מן החיצונה ולא עירב, לא מצי למיפרך הכי — דלימא דמצי מבטל בן חיצונה לבני החיצונה, ותיתי פנימית ותשתרי בהדייהו; דהכא ליכא דיורי חיצונה בפנימית אלא ע"י עירוב המרגילה — לא חשיב ביטולי רשות מחצר לחצר, כיון דמאיליהן משתרו בני חיצונה ע"י שמבטל בן פנימי לבני פנימית, כראב"י דאמר: אין צריך לבטל רשות לכל אחד וא'. אבל לעיל, דפנימית אוסרת החיצונה ע"י דריסת הרגל שלה — אע"ג דא"צ לבטל לכל אחד ואחד, חשיב ליה ביטול רשות מחצר לחצר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 67a:3:1.english: "In accordance with whose [opinion]? In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, etc." - Earlier in our discussion, when they placed their eiruv in the outer [courtyard] and one [resident] of the outer [courtyard] forgot and did not establish an eiruv, one could not object in this way — to say that the resident of the outer [courtyard] can renounce [his rights] in favor of the residents of the outer [courtyard], and the inner [courtyard] would come and be permitted along with them. For here, there is no residence of the outer [courtyard] in the inner [courtyard] except by virtue of the eiruv that gives them access [to it]; [therefore,] it is not considered renouncing rights from one courtyard to another, since the residents of the outer [courtyard] are permitted of their own accord through the resident of the inner [courtyard] renouncing [his rights] in favor of the residents of the inner [courtyard], in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, who said [that] one does not need to renounce rights to each and every [person]. However, earlier, where the inner [courtyard] prohibits the outer [courtyard] by virtue of its right of passage, even though one does not need to renounce to each and every one, it is considered renouncing rights from one courtyard to another.
